Patient  Care  Technician                      Event  Category:  Health  Professions
………………………………………………………………………………………………………………
 
Eligible  Divisions:  Secondary  &  Postsecondary/  Collegiate  
Round  One:  50  Q  test  (60  minutes)  Digital  Upload:  NO  
Solo  Event:  1  competitor  Round  Two:  Skill(s)  assessment   
New  for  2026-2027
 Editorial  changes  have  been  made.  Items  competitors  must  provide  has  been  updated.  Laboratory  Requisition  Form  
has
 
been
 
updated.
  
Event  Summary
 Patient  Care  Technician  allows  members  to  gain  the  knowledge  and  skills  required  for  patient  care  in  medical  settings.  This  
competitive
 
event
 
consists
 
of
 
two
 
rounds.
 
Round
 
One
 
is
 
a
 
written,
 
multiple-choice
 
test,
 
and
 
the
 
top-scoring
 
competitors
 
advance
 
to
 
Round
 
Two
 
for
 
the
 
skills
 
assessment.
 
This
 
event
 
aims
 
to
 
inspire
 
members
 
to
 
learn
 
more
 
about
 
the
 
ﬁeld
 
and
 
how
 
to
 
provide
 
quality
 
patient
 
care.
  
Sponsorship
 
HOSA-Future  Health  Professionals  appreciates  the  sponsorship  of  this  event  by  the  National  Healthcareer  Association. NHA  has  developed  a  special landing  page  for  competitors  and  advisors.  
 
General  Event  Information
 
General  Rules   Competitors  must  be  familiar  with  and  adhere  to  the  General  Rules  and  Regulations.  
Dress  Code  Proper  business  attire  or  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform.  Bonus  points  will  be  awarded  for  proper  dress.   ●  Round  One:  Proper  business  attire,  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform,  or  attire  appropriate  to  the  occupational  area.    ●  Round  Two:  Attire  appropriate  to  the  occupational  area. 
Competitors  Must  Provide  ●  Photo  ID both  rounds   ●  Two  #2  lead  pencils  (not  mechanical)  with  eraser  for  the  test.  ●  Neon  colored  foam  earplugs,  NOT  earbuds,  for  noise  control  (Rd1-optional)  ●  Barrier  devices  (2  pairs  of  non-latex  gloves,  gown,  goggles  or  safety  glasses,  mask)  HOSA  Conference  Staff  will  provide  equipment  and  supplies  listed  in  Appendix  I.  
Ofﬁcial  References   The  references  below  are  used  in  the  development  of  the  test  questions  and  skill  rating  sheets:  ●  National  Healthcareer  Association PCT  SKILLS  BUILDER  PLUS an  online  learning  resource  that  provides  students  with  an  interactive  learning  experience  focused  on  the  knowledge  and  skills  needed  to  be  a  Patient  Care  Technician.NHA  is  offering  HOSA  members  a  10%  discount  on  individual  purchases  and  group  discounts  by  contacting  an  NHA  sales  representative.  Visit  the  competition  landing  page  HERE. ●  National  Healthcareer  Association Certiﬁed  Patient  Care  Technician/Assistant  (CPCT/A)  Online  Study  Guide NHA’s  online  study  guide  helps  learners  prepare  for  the  Certiﬁed  Patient  Care  Technician  exam.  
 Patient  Care  Technician   ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  1  of  18  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

ROUND  ONE-  Test
 
Test  Instructions  All  competitors  will  be  given  a  test  and  answer  sheet   The  written  test  will  consist  of  50  multiple-choice  items  in  a  maximum  of  60  minutes.  See  test  instructions  here. 
Time  Remaining  Announcements  
There  will  be  NO  verbal  announcements  for  time  remaining  during  ILC  testing.  All  ILC  testing  will  be  completed  in  the  Testing  Center,  and  competitors  are  responsible  for  monitoring  their  own  time.  
Written  Test  Plan  The  written  test  for  Patient  Care  Technician  is:  ●  Patient  Care  -  44%  ●  Compliance,  Safety,  &  Professional  Responsibility  -  20%  ●  Infection  Control  -  12%  ●  Phlebotomy  -  14%  ●  EKG  -  10%  
Sample  Test  Questions  1.  When  applying  a  splint  to  an  extremity,  where  would  you  begin  the  application  according  to  proximity  guidelines?  (PCT  Skillsbuilder  Plus:  M9-Mobility  and  Transfers-Transport  Patient  via  Bed,  Stretcher,  or  Wheelchair)  A.  Start  at  the  proximal  part  of  the  extremity  and  work  towards  the  distal  part.  B.  Begin  at  the  distal  part  of  the  extremity  and  work  towards  the  proximal  part.  C.  Start  at  the  midpoint  of  the  extremity  and  work  outwards.  D.  Begin  at  the  joint  closest  to  the  torso  and  work  towards  the  ﬁngers  or  toes.  2.  A  patient  care  technician  should  identify  which  of  the  following  pieces  of  personal  protective  equipment  (PPE)  should  be  removed  ﬁrst?  (NHA-  PCT  SkillsBuilder  Plus:  M4-Patient  Safety-Infection  Control-PPE)  A.  Gloves  B.  Face  shield  C.  Mask  D.  Goggles  3.  A  patient  care  technician  is  performing  a  12-lead  EKG  for  a  patient.  In  which  of  the  following  locations  should  the  technician  place  the  V4  lead?  (NHA  -  PCT  SkillsBuilder  Plus;  M10-Advanced  Clinical  Skills-EKG)  A.  Fourth  intercostal  space,  to  the  right  of  the  sternum  B.  Fourth  intercostal  space,  to  the  left  of  the  sternum  C.  Left  anterior  axillary  line  D.  Fifth  intercostal  space  at  the  midclavicular  line   
ROUND  TWO-  Skills  Assessment
 
1.  The  top  competitors  from  Round  One  will  advance  to  Round  Two.  The  number  of  advancing  competitors  will  be  determined  by  the  scores  obtained  in  Round  One  and  the  space  and  time  available  for  Round  Two.  Round  Two  ﬁnalists  will  be  announced  on-site  at  ILC  per  the  conference  agenda.  
2.  Round  Two  is  a  selected  skill(s)  performance.  The  Round  Two  skills  approved  for  this  event  are:  Skill  I:  Discontinue  Peripheral  IV  5  minutes  
Skill  II:  Applying  Sequential  Compression  Devices  6  minutes  
Skill  III:  Measuring  an  Infant’s  Length  &  Weight  7  minutes  
Skill  IV:  Urinary  Catheter  Maintenance  5  minutes  
 Patient  Care  Technician   ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)         Page  2  of  18  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   
Skill  V:  Routine  ETS  Venipuncture  10  minutes  
Skill  VI:  Obtaining  a  12-Lead  EKG  10  minutes  
Skill  VII:  Glucometer  8  minutes  3.  For  all  skills,  body  ﬂuids  will  be  a  simulated  product.   
4.  The  selected  skill(s)  will  be  presented  to  competitors  as  a  written  scenario  at  the  beginning  of  the  round.  The  scenario  will  be  the  same  for  each  competitor.  A  sample  scenario  can  be  found here. Some  scenarios  may  involve  the  combination  of  multiple  skills.  If  the  event  rating  sheets  are  combined,  it  is  not  necessary  to  repeat  a  task  a  second  time.  An  example  would  be  competitors  would  not  need  to  identify  the  patient  twice.  
5.  Timing  will  begin  when  the  scenario  is  presented  to  the  competitors  and  will  be  stopped  at  the  end  of  the  time  allowed.  The  scenario  is  a  secret  topic.  Competitors  MAY  NOT  discuss  or  reveal  the  secret  topic  until  after  the  event  has  concluded  or  will  face  penalties  per  the  GRRs.   
6.  Competitors  must  complete  all  skill  steps  listed  in  the  guidelines,  even  if  the  steps  must  be  simulated/verbalized.  (If  the  equipment  is  available,  the  competitors  would  complete  all  skill  steps  as  the  scenario  warrants.  The  competitors  will  simulate/verbalize  the  steps  if  the  equipment  is  unavailable.)  
7.  Judges  will  provide  information  to  competitors  as  directed  by  the  rating  sheets.  Competitors  may  ask  questions  of  the  judges  while  performing  skills,  if  the  questions  relate  to  patient’s  condition  and  will  be  included  in  the  scenario  or  judge  script.  
8.  Competitors  must  use  all  equipment  correctly  and  safely.  Judges  will  stop  a  student  and  not  award  points  for  a  step  if  they  see  a  competitor  is  about  to  cause  a  risk  of  harm  or  about  to  damage  equipment  or  other  supplies.   
Final  Scoring 
 1.  The  competitor  must  earn  a  score  of  70%  or  higher  on  the  combined  skill(s)  in  Round  Two-Skills  Assessment  in  order  
to
 
be
 
recognized
 
as
 
an
 
award
 
winner
 
at
 
the
 
ILC.
 
  2.  The  ﬁnal  rank  is  determined  by  adding  the  round  one  test  score  plus  the  round  two  skill  score.  In  the  event  of  a  tie,  
the
 
highest
 
test
 
score
 
will
 
be
 
used
 
to
 
determine
 
the
 
ﬁnal
 
placement.
  
Future  Opportunities  The  HOSA  Scholarship  program  has  funding  available  for  HOSA  members  who  have  an  interest  in  various  health  careers!   The  application  process  begins  January  1,  2027,  and  can  be  found  here: https://hosa.org/scholarships/.   Graduating  from  high  school  or  completing  your  postsecondary/collegiate  program  does  not  mean  your  HOSA  journey  has  to  
end.

 Skill  I:  Discontinue  Peripheral  Intravenous  Site  Possible  Awarded  1.    Veriﬁed  physician's  orders  and  reviewed  scenario  for  any  bleeding  issues.  
      2       0  
  
2.    Obtained  needed  equipment  and  supplies.  
 1  0  
  
3.    Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
      2       0  
  
4.   Put  on  gloves.  
 2  0  
  
5.   Identiﬁed  patient  by  checking  ID  bracelet  and  asking  the  patient  to  state  their  name  and    birthdate.  
 2  0  
  
6.   Identiﬁed  self  and  explained  skill  to  patient.  
 2  0  
  
7.   Provided  privacy.  
 2  0  
  
8.   Removing  dressing:  a.  Removed  overlying  tape.  
 1  0  
  
b.  Removed  transparent  membrane  dressing  by  picking  up  one  corner  and  pulling  the  side  laterally  while  holding  the  catheter  hub.  
2  0  
  
c.  Repeated  pulling  dressing  from  the  other  side  laterally  while  holding  catheter  hub.  
2  0  
  
d.  Alternatively,  remove  gauze  dressing  and  tape  one  layer  at  a  time.  
2  0  
  
e.  Tape  securing  catheter  to  skin  left  intact.  
2  0  
  
9.   Turned  IV  tubing  roller  clamp  to  “off”  position  and  removed  tape  securing  tubing.  
2  0  
  
10.   Removed  IV  dressing  and  tape  while  stabilizing  catheter.  
2  0  
  
11.   Held  dry  gauze  over  site.  
1  0  
  
12.   Applied  light  pressure  and  withdrew  the  catheter  using  a  slow  steady  movement.  
2  0  
  
13.   The  hub  remained  parallel  to  the  skin  while  removing.  
2  0  
  
14.   Using  the  dry,  sterile  gauze,  applied  pressure  to  the  site  for  2  to  3  minutes.  
2  0  
  
15.   Secured  tape  snugly  over  the  gauze.  
1  0  
  
16.   Inspected  the  catheter  for  intactness,  noting  tip  integrity  and  length.  
2  0  
  
17.    Discarded  used  supplies.  
1  0  
  
18.    Removed  gloves  and  washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  
19.    Instructed  patient  to  report  any  erythema,  pain,  drainage,  or  edema  that  occurs  after  catheter   removal  
2  0  
  
20.   Document  the  following::  a.  Time  peripheral  IV  infusion  was  discontinued.  
2  0

 Skill  II:  Applying  Sequential  Compression  Devices  Possible  Awarded      1.    Assembled  equipment  and  supplies.  
1  0  
  
    2.    Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol  based  hand-rub  for  hand  hygiene. 
2  0  
  
3.    Identiﬁed  patient  by  checking  ID  bracelet  and  asking  patient  to  state  their  name  and     birthdate.  
2  0  
  
4.   Identiﬁed  self  and  explained  the  procedure  to  the  patient.  
2  0  
  
5.   Provided  privacy.  
2  0  
  
6.   Arranged  sequential  compression  device  (SCD)  sleeve  under  patient’s  leg  according  to  leg   position  indicated  on  the  inner  lining  of  sleeve.  a.  Back  of  patient’s  ankle  should  line  up  with  ankle  on  inner  lining  of  sleeve.  
2  0  
  
 b.  Positioned  back  of  knee  with  popliteal  opening.  
2  0  
  
7.   Wrapped  SCD  sleeve  securely  around  patient’s  leg.  
2  0  
  
8.   Veriﬁed  ﬁt  of  SCD  sleeves  by  placing  two  ﬁngers  between  patient’s  legs  and  sleeves.  
2  0  
  
9.   Attached  connector  of  SCD  sleeve  to  plug  on  mechanical  unit  using  arrow  on  plug.  
1  0  
  
10.   Turned  unit  on  and  veriﬁed  is  functioning.  
1  0  
  
11.   Observed  the  functioning  of  the  unit  for  one  full  cycle.  
1  0  
  
12.   Repositioned  patient  for  comfort.  
1  0  
  
13.   Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol  based  hand-rub  for  hand  hygiene.  
1  0  
  
14.   Documented  in  nursing  notes.  
2  0  
  
15.   Used  appropriate  verbal  and  nonverbal  communication  with  patient.  
2  0  
  
16.   Practiced  standard  precautions  throughout  skill.  
2  0

Patient  Care  Technician  Skill  III:  Measuring  an  Infant’s  Length  &  Weight
 
Time:  7  minutes  Competitor   #: ___________________________    Division:  ________ SS  ________ PS/C     Judge’s  Signature: ________________________
 
 Skill  III:  Measuring  an  Infant’s  Length  &  Weight  Possible  Awarded      1.    Assembled  equipment  and  supplies.  
1  0  
  
    2.    Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol  based  hand-rub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  
3.    Identiﬁed  patient  by  checking  ID  bracelet  and  asking  patient/caregiver  to  state  their  name   and  birthdate.  
2  0  
  
4.   Identiﬁed  self  and  explained  skill  to  the  infant’s  caregiver.  
2  0  
  
5.   Prepared  the  scale  by  lining  it  with  disposable  paper.  
2  0  
  
6.   Provided  privacy.  
2  0  
  
7.   Asked  the  caregiver  to  place  the  infant  on  their  back  on  the  examination  paper.  
1  0  
  
8.   Undressed  infant  -  diaper  may  be  left  on  for  length  measurement.  
1  0  
  
9.   Asked  the  caregiver  to  hold  their  head  still  gently.  
1  0  
  
10.   Straightened  one  leg.  
1  0  
  
11.   Marked  on  examination  paper  at  the  top  of  the  infant’s  head  and  at  the  heel  after  the  leg  is   extended.  
1  0  
  
12.   Measured  the  length  between  marks  on  exam  paper  with  a  tape  measure  and  recorded.  
2  0  
  
13.   Removed  diaper.  
1  0  
  
14.   Placed  the  infant  gently  on  the  scale  keeping  hand  above  the  infant’s  trunk  for  safety.  
2  0  
  
15.   Recorded  weight.  
2  0  
  
16.   Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol  based  hand-rub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  
17    Recorded  length  and  weight  on  the  Nurses  Notes.  
2  0  
  
18.    Completed  growth  chart  for  both  height  and  weight  by  connecting  dots  from  last  visit.  
2  0  
  
19.   Used  appropriate  verbal  and  nonverbal  communication  with  patient.  
2  0  
  
20.   Practiced  standard  precautions  throughout  skill.  
2  0

Time:  5  minutes  Competitor   #: ___________________________      Division:  ________ SS  ________ PS/C    Judge’s  Signature: ________________________  *The  scenario  will  include  the  gender  of  the  patient  requiring  urinary  catheter  maintenance.  
 Skill  IV:  Urinary  Catheter  Maintenance  Possible  Awarded      1.    Assembled  equipment  and  supplies.  
1  0  
      2.    Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  3.    Approached,  greeted  the  patient,  and  identiﬁed  self.  
1  0  
  4.   Identiﬁed  patient  by  checking  ID  bracelet  and  asking  patient  to  state  their  name  and    birthdate.  
2  0  
  
5.    Explained  the  procedure  and  obtained  consent.  
2  0  
  6.   Provided  privacy.  
2  0  
  7.   Applied  gloves.  
2  0  
  8.   POSITIONED  PATIENT:   FEMALE:  Dorsal  recumbent  position,  OR   MALE:  Supine  with  legs  extended  and  thighs  slightly  abducted  
2  0  
  
9.   Placed  a  waterproof  pad  under  the  patient.  
1  0  
  10.   Performed  perineal  care  using  soap  and  water  with  a  washcloth,  or  other  cleansing  agent    speciﬁed  by  facility.  (scenario)  
2  0  
  11.   Cleaned  catheter  tubing  moving  away  from  the  body.  
2  0  
  12.   Evaluate,  observe  and  verbalize  (to  judge)  any  changes  or  discomfort  including:  discharge,   length  of  time  catheter  has  been  in  place,  inﬂammation,  edema,  changes  in  tissue  color,    burning.  
2  0  
  
13.   Secure  catheter  to  patient’s  leg  and  collection  device  to  bed  of  frame  below  the     patient’s  bladder.  
2  0  
  14.   Removed  gloves.  
1  0  
  15.   Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  16.   Used  appropriate  verbal  and  nonverbal  communication  with  patient  and  other  personnel.  
2  0  
  17.   Practiced  standard  precautions  throughout  skill.

 Skill  V:   Routine  ETS  Venipuncture  Possible  Awarded      1.    Reviewed  test  request/requisition  (via  the  competition  scenario).  
2  0  
  
2.    Assembled  equipment  and  supplies.  
1  0  
  
    3.    Approached,  greeted  the  patient,  and  identiﬁed  self.  
2  0  
  
4.   Identiﬁed  patient  by  checking  ID  bracelet  and  asking  the  patient  to  state  their  name  and    birthdate.  
2  0  
  
5.   Verbally  matched  the  patient  identiﬁcation  to  the  requisition.  
2  0  
  
6.   Explained  the  procedure  and  obtained  consent.  
2  0  
  
7.   Sanitized  hands  and  put  on  gloves.  
2  0  
  
8.   Attached  the  needle  ﬁrmly  to  the  Vacutainer  holder  with  cover  still  on  the  needle.  
2  0  
  
9.   Applied  tourniquet  3  to  4  inches  above  the  venipuncture,  feeling  slightly  tight  but  not    cutting  off  blood  ﬂow  in  the  artery.  
2  0  
  
10.   Asked  the  patient  to  make  a  ﬁst.  
1  0  
  
11.   Selected  the  vein  in  the  antecubital  area  by  palpating  with  the  tip  of  the  index  ﬁnger  to    trace  the  path  of  the  vein  and  judge  the  depth.  
1  0  
  
12.   Released  tourniquet,  and  asked  patient  to  open  the  ﬁst.  
1  0  
  
13.   Cleaned  selected  puncture  site  with  a  70%  isopropyl  alcohol  or  antiseptic  wipe  using  a  circle   motion  starting  at  the  center  and  working  outward  in  a  circular  pattern.  
2  0  
  
14.   Allowed  the  site  to  air  dry  for  up  to  60  seconds  before  proceeding.  
1  0  
  
15.   Reapplied  the  tourniquet  and  asked  the  patient  to  make  a  ﬁst.  
1  0  
  
16.   Held  the  Vacutainer  assembly  in  dominant  hand  with  thumb  on  top  and  ﬁngers    underneath.  
1  0  
  
17.   Placed  ﬁrst  tube  in  vacutainer  without  pushing  into  the  double-pointed  needle.  
1  0  
  
18.   Removed  the  needle  sheath.  
1  0  
  
19.   Used  the  thumb  on  the  nondominant  hand  to  anchor  the  vein  by  stretching  the  skin    downward  below  the  puncture  site.  
1  0  
  
20.   With  bevel  up,  aligned  parallel  to  vein  and  inserted  needle  at  a  15  to  30  degree  angle    into  the  vein  in  quick  smooth  motion.  
1  0  
  
21.   Placed  two  ﬁngers  on  the  ﬂanges  of  the  needle  holder,  and  used  thumb  to  engage  the  tube    with  the  double-pointed  needle.  
1  0  
  
22.   Ensured  the  needle  did  not  change  positions  in  the  vein.  
1  0  
  
23.   When  blood  began  to  ﬂow,  directed  the  patient  to  release  their  ﬁst.    
1  0

Skill  V:  Continued…  Possible  Awarded  24.   Allowed  tube  to  ﬁll  to  maximum  capacity  
1  0  
  
25.   Removed  the  tube  by  curling  the  ﬁngers  underneath  and  pushing  on  the  needle  holder    with  the  thumb  while  taking  care  not  to  move  needle  in  the  vein.  
1  0  
  
26.   Repeated  steps  above  for  ﬁlling  remaining  tubes.  
1  0  
  
27.   Gently  inverted  tubes  after  removing  to  mix  anticoagulants  and  blood.  
1  0  
  
28.   As  the  last  tube  is  ﬁlling,  release  the  tourniquet.  
1  0  
  
29.   When  the  last  tube  has  ﬁlled,  remove  the  tube  from  the  needle.  
1  0  
  
30.   Removed  the  last  tube  from  the  holder.  
1  0  
  
31.   Placed  gauze  over  the  puncture  site.  
1  0  
  
32.   Quickly  removed  needle  and  engaged  safety  device.  
2  0  
  
33.   Disposed  of  the  entire  unit  in  a  sharps  container.  
2  0  
  
34.   Instructed  patient  to  maintain  pressure  on  venipuncture  site  until  bleeding  stops  and  to    not  bend  the  elbow.  
2  0  
  
35.   Labeled  and  prepared  tubes  for  handling  and  transport  before  leaving  patient.  
1  0  
  
36.   Checked  the  puncture  site  for  bleeding  and  hematoma  formation.  
2  0  
  
37.   Applied  a  hypoallergenic  bandage.  
1  0  
  
38.   Disinfected  work  area.  
2  0  
  
39.   Disposed  of  used  materials.  
2  0  
  
40.   Removed  and  disposed  of  gloves.  
2  0  
  
41.   Washed  hands  or  used  alcohol-based  handrub  for  hand  hygiene.  
2  0  
  
42.   Completed  requisition  and  documented  in  the  patient's  chart.  
2  0  
  
43.   Verbalized  specimen  would  be  routed  to  appropriate  place.  
2  0  
  
44.   Used  appropriate  verbal  and  nonverbal  communication  with  patient  and  other  personnel.  
2  0  
  
45.   Tourniquet  did  not  remain  on  arm  for  greater  than  120  seconds  during  site  selection.  
2  0  
  
46.   Practiced  standard  precautions  throughout  skill.  
2  0
